why: One corpus, read from both sides of the wire, because two parsers have to agree about it and neither
of them can check the other from where it runs.
`sent` is what this console sends. `app.admin.apply.parse_document` runs PyYAML, whose reading goes to
the API server as JSON, and since ADR-0009 the browser reads the same document the same way, against
the mirror schema in `frontend/src/components/clusterYaml.js`. So the two columns are not two opinions
the console holds -- they are one reading and the reading of the YAML version most editors implement.
`yaml12` is what js-yaml's default schema makes of the scalar: YAML 1.2's core schema, which is the
spec, what the operator's editor almost certainly implements, and what colours the text on the way
here. Where it differs from `sent`, the console says so -- `diverges` is that set, and it is derived
rather than asserted so a reader can see its shape at a glance.
Who checks what. `backend/tests/test_yaml_scalar_reading.py` asserts PyYAML still reads every row as
`sent`, which is what catches a PyYAML release that moves one. `frontend/tests/e2e/cluster-yaml.spec.js`
asserts two things against the same rows: that js-yaml's default schema reads them as `yaml12`, and
that the mirror reads them as `sent` -- and that a form edit dumped by the mirror parses back to the
same value, because a round trip that does not is a form edit that changes a field nobody opened.
Values are written as JSON, with three spellings JSON has no literal for: "@inf", "@-inf" and "@nan".
Those three rows are the ones `parse_document` refuses outright -- JSON cannot carry them and the API
server is sent JSON -- so what the corpus records for them is the reading, not a body that goes anywhere.
One distinction is deliberately absent. Python has an int and a float where JavaScript has one number,
so PyYAML reading `1.` as 1.0 and js-yaml reading it as 1 is a difference the mirror cannot represent
and no check here claims to catch. It is also not a difference that reaches a cluster: both are the
number one, and JSON spells them the same.
A third reading exists and is not in this file: `kubectl`'s, which is neither of these columns. It is
recorded in `docs/adr-0009-one-yaml-reading.md` with the library version it came from, because no test
in this repository can run it and a column nothing asserts is a column that rots.
